correctness.rationale: For every finite partition, every t_i in [1,2] and every real zero-sum mass, sum_i U_i=2P proves at most one overloaded part. Fractional Hall gives a fully cross-part coupling in the balanced case; explicit routing into and out of the unique overloaded part leaves precisely U_i-P internal mass in the other case. A sign-based 1-Lipschitz potential attains P in the balanced case; explicit four-level values t_i,0,1,t_i-1 attain P+(t_i-1)(U_i-P) in the overloaded case. Thus analytic primal and dual bounds coincide for all real parameters and endpoint cases. The coupling construction is independent of every t_i; affine norm interpolation follows. Standard-library exact arithmetic independently checks 745 instances and 745 interpolations; finite checks are not substituted for proof.

This yields a global pointwise affine deformation of finite Lipschitz-free norms, an explicit transport plan, and a single overloaded-part certificate.
